record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Existence for mark-based cognitive map model
record.original_question: Consider the coupled system with moving populations and dynamically evolving landscape marks, where u_i satisfies ∂_t u_i = d_iΔu_i − γ_i∇·(u_i∇p_i g,R) and p_i satisfies ∂_t p_i = Σ_j=1^n α_ij u_j − μp_i. With periodic boundary conditions on a bounded domain and a top-hat detection function, in what sense do time-dependent solutions exist, and do they remain well defined in the local limit R → 0+?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6. In what sense do solutions exist solving the time-dependent problem (2.11) subject to periodic boundary conditions and a top-hat detection function in a bounded domain? Do solutions remain well defined in the limit as R → 0+?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions. For $n \geq 1$, consider $n$ population densities $u_i(x,t) \geq 0$ and $n$ associated landscape "mark" fields $p_i(x,t) \geq 0$, $i=1,\dots,n$, evolving according to the coupled system
$$\partial_t u_i = d_i \Delta u_i - \gamma_i \nabla \cdot \!\bigl(u_i \, \nabla \overline{p_i}^{\,g,R}\bigr), \qquad x \in \Omega,\ t>0,$$
$$\partial_t p_i = \sum_{j=1}^n \alpha_{ij}\, u_j - \mu\, p_i, \qquad x \in \Omega,\ t>0,$$
together with initial data $u_i(\cdot,0)=u_i^0 \geq 0$, $p_i(\cdot,0)=p_i^0 \geq 0$ and periodic boundary conditions on $\Omega$. Here $d_i>0$, $\gamma_i \in \mathbb{R}$, $\mu>0$, and $\alpha_{ij} \in \mathbb{R}$ are constants. The nonlocal average $\overline{p_i}^{\,g,R}$ is defined by convolution against the top-hat detection kernel of radius $R>0$,
$$\overline{p_i}^{\,g,R}(x,t) \;=\; \frac{1}{|B_R(0)|}\int_{B_R(0)} p_i(x+y,t)\,dy,$$
extended periodically in $x$.

(a) Determine in what functional sense (e.g., classical, strong, weak, mild, or measure-valued) time-dependent solutions $(u_i,p_i)_{i=1}^n$ of this system exist, globally in time, for a non-smooth top-hat detection kernel.

(b) Determine whether such solutions remain well defined in the local limit $R \to 0^+$, and characterize the limiting problem (or obstruction to passing to the limit).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work establishes existence and uniqueness of Hölder-continuous weak solutions in one spatial dimension for related single- and multi-species nonlocal advection-diffusion models with discontinuous top-hat detection kernels, and shows that solutions can blow up as the detection radius shrinks to zero, indicating that nonlocality is essential for global existence. Thus part (a) is partially resolved (notably in 1D and certain multi-species settings), while the local limit $R \to 0^+$ in part (b) generally fails to be well posed; a fully general resolution for the coupled mark-based system on bounded periodic domains in arbitrary dimension does not appear to be established.

status_evidence.title: Local and Global Existence for Nonlocal Multispecies Advection-Diffusion Models
status_evidence.snippet: Existence theory for multispecies nonlocal advection-diffusion systems with general (including top-hat) detection kernels.
status_evidence.claim: Existence results have been obtained for related multispecies nonlocal advection-diffusion systems.

status_evidence.title: Biological Aggregations from Spatial Memory and Nonlocal Advection
status_evidence.snippet: Coupled PDE-ODE systems with top-hat kernel; solutions can blow up in finite time when the detection radius becomes zero.
status_evidence.claim: The local limit R → 0 is generally not well posed; solutions may blow up.

status_evidence.title: Positivity and global existence for nonlocal advection-diffusion models of interacting populations
status_evidence.snippet: Global existence and positivity for nonlocal advection-diffusion models of interacting populations.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on global existence for related coupled systems.
